accuracy.claim: One Django project: one app per feature area (accounts, api, front, logs, payments) and one per integration kind, each in INSTALLED_APPS and routed from hc/urls.py.
accuracy.note: INSTALLED_APPS lists the five feature apps and 30 integration apps; hc/urls.py includes every app's URL module. hc.logs has no views, so it has no URL module to route.

accuracy.claim: Server-rendered templates with small jQuery scripts; pages update by polling HTML-fragment or JSON endpoints; no SPA, build step, websocket or server push.
accuracy.note: base.html loads jquery-3.6.0; log.js, details.js, checks.js and projects.js poll through adaptiveSetInterval; no WebSocket or EventSource anywhere. Static bundles come from 'manage.py compress' (offline django-compressor), not from a JavaScript toolchain.

accuracy.claim: All state lives in one relational database reached through the ORM on SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB alike; numbered migrations; no engine-specific behaviour; queries sort by created, not id.
accuracy.note: The ORM over four engines (DB env var, CI matrix on all four), migrations and the sort-by-created comments hold. Wrong detail: 'all state' is not in that one database. With S3_BUCKET set, Check.ping stores ping bodies over 100 bytes in object storage (object_size plus put_object), and docs_search reads a separate SQLite file (search.db) through sqlite3.

accuracy.claim: Alert delivery is a pull model with no broker: a status-change row is written and the separate sendalerts process polls unprocessed rows and delivers them; no scheduler, no retry table.
accuracy.note: The create_flip docstring states it, and process_one_flip polls Flip(processed=None). Omission: the smtpd process also records pings and so writes status changes, besides the web and alert processes.

accuracy.claim: Work is claimed with optimistic conditional UPDATEs that must change exactly one row (flip processed, check status, report next date); lost races are skipped.
accuracy.note: process_one_flip runs update(processed=now()) guarded on processed=None, handle_going_down guards on the old status, and handle_one_report and handle_one_nag guard on the next date. Each skips when num_updated != 1.

accuracy.claim: Delivery is at most once per status change and integration: marked processed before contact, failures never re-queued, an escaped exception or crash abandons the remaining integrations; retries only inside one attempt.
accuracy.note: processed is set before executor.submit, an exception from ch.notify leaves the channel loop in notify(), and nothing re-queues. Edge cases: a channel assigned directly and also as a group member is notified twice for one status change, and in-attempt HTTP tries can reach the remote more than once.

accuracy.claim: sendalerts is one long-running command: 2 s idle sleep, thread pool of --num-workers (default 1), signal handlers let deliveries finish, stale connections closed per thread, application name set; the Docker container stops when any child exits.
accuracy.note: Holds: time.sleep(2), ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_workers), the SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers followed by executor.shutdown(wait=True), close_old_connections, application_name 'sendalerts'. docker/run.sh ends with 'wait -n'; the README and CHANGELOG v5.0 support it.

accuracy.claim: One transport class per kind registered in TRANSPORTS and imported on first use; implements notify(flip, notification) and is_noop(status); HTTP kinds extend HttpTransport, Slack-compatible kinds extend Slackalike.
accuracy.note: Channel.transport imports the dotted path and caches the class in TRANSPORTS. Slack, Discord and Mattermost extend Slackalike; the other HTTP kinds extend HttpTransport.

accuracy.claim: Delivery errors are TransportError(message, permanent): message stored and shown verbatim; permanent disables the integration and ends in-attempt retries; other exceptions propagate.
accuracy.note: Channel.notify catches only TransportError, stores e.message and sets disabled when the error is permanent. HttpTransport.request and Signal stop retrying on a permanent error.

accuracy.claim: One attempt is one Notification row inserted with error 'Sending' before sending and finalized afterwards; callbacks address it by its random code; Channel last_notify, last_notify_duration and last_error summarize the latest attempt.
accuracy.note: n.save() runs before transport.notify, then the code updates error. notification_status and bounces look the row up by code. Channel fields are overwritten after every attempt.

accuracy.claim: Channel.notify is the single entry point for one delivery and returns '' / 'no-op' / error text; sendalerts, the Test! view, the group transport and the account-deletion command call it.
accuracy.note: A grep finds exactly these four callers (sendalerts.notify, send_test_notification, Group.notify, senddeletionscheduled), and each reads the returned string.

accuracy.claim: Retrying is per transport inside one attempt: HttpTransport up to 3 immediate tries, Signal 2, email 3 with 1 s pause; opt-out via permanent errors and for webhook tests; no policy object, back-off, stored counter or setting.
accuracy.note: tries_left = 3 if retry else 1 with no sleep; Signal tries_left = 2; EmailThread MAX_TRIES = 3 with time.sleep(1). The webhook passes retry=False when notification.owner is None. The webhook form promises 'up to 2 additional times'.

accuracy.claim: Quotas and rate limits are enforced inside each transport at send time via profile counters and TokenBucket rows; a refusal is an ordinary failed attempt, so each call spends quota.
accuracy.note: SMS and WhatsApp call authorize_sms and Call calls authorize_call before posting. Telegram, Signal, Pushover and ntfy use TokenBucket.authorize_*. Refusals raise a non-permanent TransportError.

accuracy.claim: The event log is assembled per request from pings, notifications and flips, merged and sorted in Python, rendered by shared row templates for the Events page, its fragment and the details page; no unified event table.
accuracy.note: _get_events builds pings + alerts + flips and sorts them with key (created, isinstance Flip). log_rows.html and details_events.html both include log_row.html.

accuracy.claim: Notification and flip retention derives from ping retention (ping_log_limit, default 100), runs inline every 100th ping plus an optional batch command; no separate retention setting.
accuracy.note: Check.ping calls prune() when n_pings % 100 == 0, and prunepingsslow prunes checks with more than 100 pings. Flips are kept for min(oldest ping, 93 days); the '~3 months of flips' comment is quoted correctly.

accuracy.claim: Per-project authorization in views through helpers (superuser, owner, membership; no membership 404; member and manager read-write; mutating views 403); API keys stored as HMAC-SHA256 digest with an 8-character prefix, plain-text keys still accepted.
accuracy.note: _get_*_for_user use get_object_or_404(Member), is_rw covers REGULAR and MANAGER, and _get_rw_* raise PermissionDenied. _make_api_key stores secret[:8] + '.' + HMAC-SHA256 hex; for_api_key also matches plain-text keys.

accuracy.claim: Callbacks from third parties are CSRF-exempt, unauthenticated endpoints whose only credential is an unguessable record code or a short-lived signed identifier (1 h status callbacks, 48 h bounces); missing or expired identifiers get HTTP 200.
accuracy.note: True for the delivery callbacks. notification_status (csrf_exempt, record code, 1 h cutoff) and bounces (csrf_exempt, signed id with max_age 48 h) both answer 200 when the identifier is missing or expired. Wrong detail: the claim covers every third-party callback, but the Telegram bot webhook (hc/integrations/telegram/views.py telegram_bot) is csrf_exempt and checks no identifier or signature at all, and OAuth completions such as Slack add_complete are login_required and check a session state.

accuracy.claim: Configuration from environment variables via envbool/envint/envsecret (_FILE), overridden by local settings; integration availability checked when added and at send time; sanity problems are system checks; every setting is documented in the settings reference.
accuracy.note: The env helpers, the local_settings override, require_setting on add views plus the transport checks, and settings_check all hold. Wrong detail: EMAIL_MAIL_FROM_TMPL, METRICS_KEY, STATSD_HOST, SUPPORT_EMAIL and USE_GZIP_MIDDLEWARE are read from the environment in hc/settings.py but are absent from templates/docs/self_hosted_configuration.md. The baseline's own R-4 b9 flags EMAIL_MAIL_FROM_TMPL, and R-16 b6 (outside the sample) repeats the overstatement.

accuracy.claim: Expected failures are data (record error, last error, statsd counters, process log lines); unexpected exceptions go to the hc logger, whose handler writes database rows; Django emails ADMINS about request errors.
accuracy.note: LOGGING routes hc.* and django.request to hc.logs.Handler, and sendalerts logs 'Exception in notify'. Some expected failures are also logged as exceptions: the email transport calls logger.exception on SMTP errors and Signal on socket errors. So R-14 b5 (outside the sample), which says they are not, is wrong.

accuracy.claim: All outbound integration HTTP goes through hc.lib.curl.request: HTTP/HTTPS only, at most 3 redirects, 30 s timeout from HttpTransport, private addresses refused unless INTEGRATIONS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS; Apprise is the documented exception.
accuracy.note: Holds: PROTOCOLS HTTP|HTTPS, MAXREDIRS 3, the opensocket check and timeout=30. The OAuth views and the GitHub and Matrix clients also use curl. The settings reference names Apprise as the exception.

accuracy.claim: Code-running or internal-reaching capabilities are opt-in (SHELL_ENABLED off by default); webhook placeholders are substituted without re-expanding values.
accuracy.note: SHELL_ENABLED, APPRISE_ENABLED and INTEGRATIONS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS default to False. hc.lib.string.replace replaces only placeholders that appear in the template.

accuracy.claim: Integration configuration is text in Channel.value whose format depends on the kind (bare string, delimited string, JSON parsed through pydantic models and typed dictionaries such as WebhookSpec and EmailConf); no per-kind table.
accuracy.note: Pushover splits on '|', group on ','; WebhookSpec, EmailConf and the other *Conf classes are pydantic models. Minor: no TypedDicts parse configuration; Slack and Discord read plain json.loads dicts.

accuracy.claim: Integration code is replicated per kind; a new kind copies a similar one; shared behaviour sits in base classes only where several kinds agree.
accuracy.note: CONTRIBUTING: 'pick a similar existing integration ... and replicate every aspect of it'. Slackalike is shared by Slack, Discord and Mattermost.

accuracy.claim: Docs are Markdown under templates/docs rendered by render_docs into committed .html-fragment files, indexed into search.db by populate_searchdb, served from fragments with placeholder substitution.
accuracy.note: 35 fragments are tracked. serve_doc reads the fragment and calls _replace_placeholders, and Markdown sits in requirements-dev.txt.

accuracy.claim: Django test runner, one tests/ package per app; CI on SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB with Python 3.12-3.15 plus mypy --strict and coverage; TransactionTestCase appears once.
accuracy.note: tests.yml matrix, mypy.yml and coverage.yml hold, and NotifyTestCase is the only TransactionTestCase. hc/payments, a placeholder app, has no tests package.

accuracy.claim: Static typing enforced: every module starts with 'from __future__ import annotations' and the tree passes mypy --strict with django-stubs; formatting is ruff.
accuracy.note: mypy.yml runs 'mypy --strict --show-traceback hc' with the plugin from mypy.ini. Minor: four code modules lack the __future__ import (hc/api/middleware.py, hc/lib/urls.py, hc/front/templatetags/asciitable.py, hc/integrations/github/client.py).

accuracy.claim: User-visible changes go into CHANGELOG.md under the top '## v...' heading; the displayed version is read from the first such heading at start-up.
accuracy.note: settings.VERSION comes from the first '## v' line. The site_version tag shows it in base.html and in the admin.

accuracy.claim: A check going down or up is recorded as a status change; alerts are made from that record, not directly from the ping or timeout.
accuracy.note: Check.ping and handle_going_down create Flip rows; sendalerts alerts only from unprocessed flips.

accuracy.claim: Before contacting the integration a record is stored with check (empty for tests), integration, new status, creation time, random code and error 'Sending'.
accuracy.note: Channel.notify sets owner unless is_test, check_status and error='Sending', and calls save() before transport.notify. code defaults to uuid4.

accuracy.claim: HTTP integrations treat any response other than 200, 201, 202, 204 or 205 as a failure 'Received status code N' (some add detail).
accuracy.note: HttpTransport._request calls raise_for_response for any other code. Several transports override it with more detail.

accuracy.claim: Within one attempt an HTTP integration makes up to 3 tries back to back with no delay and stops at the first permanent error.
accuracy.note: request() sets tries_left = 3 (1 when retry=False), has no sleep, and a permanent error sets tries_left = 0. test_webhooks_handle_500 asserts 3 calls. Per request: the Pushover recovery path sends a cancel request and the alert, each with its own tries.

accuracy.claim: Providers and mail systems report failures after the attempt; the report updates the same notification record and never creates one.
accuracy.note: notification_status and bounces fetch the existing Notification by code and call save(update_fields=['error']).

accuracy.claim: SMS and WhatsApp share one monthly counter per account owner, calls have their own; the counter rises before the provider call and is not reversed on failure.
accuracy.note: Sms and WhatsApp call owner_profile.authorize_sms and Call calls authorize_call; each saves the counter before self.post and never decrements it. test_it_works asserts sms_sent == 1.

accuracy.claim: The Events page is /checks/<code>/log/; first rows render with the page, later rows come from /checks/<code>/log_events/.
accuracy.note: check_urls has 'log/' and 'log_events/'. log.html includes log_rows.html, and log.js fetches data-refresh-url.

accuracy.claim: The initial page lists pings and status changes only; notifications appear after ticking 'Downtime alert', which starts unticked.
accuracy.note: log() calls _get_events with kinds=None, which skips notifications. The 'Downtime alert' checkbox has no 'checked' attribute while the others do.

accuracy.claim: Only 'down' notifications are ever listed; recovery ('up') alerts are not.
accuracy.note: _get_events filters check_status='down'. The details page's list never includes notifications.

accuracy.claim: A notification row has an alert icon, the creation time formatted in the selected time zone, and a one-line description.
accuracy.note: log_row.html renders ic-alert and event_summary.html, and formatPingDates fills the date and time cells. The zone is the one picked in the page's switcher (UTC, the profile zone, or a cron check's zone), not the browser's own zone.

accuracy.claim: The live poll's success handler calls the formatter with an undefined identifier dateFormat while the formatter takes one argument, so prepending new rows probably throws (inferred).
accuracy.note: log.js line 115 calls formatPingDates(dateFormat, ...), and formatPingDates(rows) takes one argument. 'dateFormat' is defined nowhere in static/js or templates, so a ReferenceError fires before prepend, after lastUpdated has already advanced.

accuracy.claim: Notifications older than the check's oldest retained ping are deleted when the check prunes (every 100th ping and the batch command).
accuracy.note: prune() deletes notification_set entries older than the earliest ping, and test_it_prunes asserts the deletion. The ping path and prunepingsslow both call prune().

accuracy.claim: The Integrations page shows Disabled / Unconfirmed / Ready to deliver and the last attempt as Delivered or Failed with time ago (error as tooltip) or Never.
accuracy.note: channels.html has exactly these branches, with the tooltip title showing ch.last_error.

accuracy.claim: Without the alert process no alerts are sent; unprocessed status changes wait in the database.
accuracy.note: self_hosted.md: 'When sendalerts is not running, the Healthchecks instance will not send out any alerts.' Flips keep processed=None until claimed.

accuracy.claim: A delivery record has a unique random code, optional check, status of at most 6 characters, integration, creation time (default now) and error text of at most 200 characters.
accuracy.note: The Notification model matches field for field: UUID unique code, nullable owner FK, CharField(6), channel FK, created default now, CharField(200).

coverage.note: AD-4 says pull model, no broker, no scheduler; AD-7 says long-running sendalerts, 2 s idle sleep, thread pool; the Interfaces 'Processes' line rules out a broker, cache or task queue. The Stack line's 'scheduling libraries cronsim and oncalendar' compute check schedules, not jobs, and could be misread.
Each integration is its own app with a transport class, and configuration lives in Channel.value through pydantic models with no per-kind table. AD-23 quotes 'replicate every aspect'.
AD-2 records server-rendered templates with no SPA. django-compressor in offline mode is named in the Stack section.
AD-3 records the ORM over SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB with no engine-specific code, and R-18 b2 names SQLite as the default. The DB variable that selects the engine is not named.
One Notification row per attempt (code, channel, created, 200-character error), and Channel.last_error holds the latest error.
Tries happen inline within one attempt, the webhook does not retry test sends, there is no back-off, and nothing re-queues.

AD-26 covers ruff and mypy --strict with django-stubs; AD-25 covers Django tests per app. 'Prefer simplicity' and 'add a test with every fix or feature' sit in the Conventions process rules and in AD-26's Why.

examples: R-8 b9: names the test module hc/front/tests/test_log.py
R-10 b4: names the identifier dateFormat, the static/js directory and JavaScript
R-16 b1: names the module hc/local_settings.py
R-16 b2: 'Apprise (flag and library)' names a library (borderline)
R-17 b7: names the HMAC algorithm
R-18 b2: names Python and the four database engines
R-18 b3: names Django migrations, hc/api/migrations and manage.py migrate

Architecture restating behaviour (most of the entry repeats spec bullets): AD-15 (R-12 b1, b2, b4 retention), AD-17 (R-4 b2, b7 and R-17 b7: 1 h / 48 h windows, HTTP 200), AD-21 (R-16 b2, R-17 b3, R-17 b6)

AD-8: Why is labelled stated (CONTRIBUTING.md 'Developing a New Integration'), but that section lists steps and gives no reason such as 'a uniform contract lets the alert process treat every kind alike'; it should be inferred.

summary: Reliable: the delivery-path decisions (claim before send, one Notification row per attempt finalized from 'Sending', per-transport in-attempt retries with no delay or stored counter, the polling sendalerts loop, the event log assembled per request) and all 15 sampled requirement bullets match the code, including the down-only, unticked-by-default 'Downtime alert' listing and the undefined dateFormat that breaks the Events page's live update. Wrong: three decisions overgeneralize: AD-3 puts all state in one ORM database (ping bodies can go to S3; docs search reads a separate search.db), AD-17 gives all third-party callbacks the record-code or signed-identifier credential (the Telegram webhook checks none, OAuth completions use the session), and AD-18 says every setting is documented (EMAIL_MAIL_FROM_TMPL, METRICS_KEY, STATSD_HOST, SUPPORT_EMAIL and USE_GZIP_MIDDLEWARE are not); outside the sample, R-16 b6 repeats that claim and R-14 b5 misses that the email and Signal transports log expected failures as exceptions. Missing: none of the seven expected facts is absent (only the DB variable that selects the engine goes unnamed), but 8 requirement bullets name implementation (Django, Python, HMAC, module paths, a JavaScript identifier), 3 decisions mostly restate spec behaviour, and AD-8's 'stated' reason is not stated by its source.
